summary: Intermittent p95 latency spikes and 502s during region-pin refresh when customer NAT causes hairpin routing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BrightCart) on a Private deployment reports intermittent P95 latency spikes up to 1.8s (baseline ~230ms) and occasional 502 gateway errors when their deployments undergo a "pin refresh" window.

Impact:
- Intermittent user-facing errors for BrightCart checkout API (approx 2-3% of requests during refresh windows).
- Increased p95 latency impacting SLIs and degrading user experience for EU customers.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering) in eu-west region.
- Customer uses their own NAT gateway / egress path for auditability (customer-managed NAT).
- Model traffic: redwood-v1-7B for embeddings, redwood-chat-13B for chat flows.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Send steady load (50 rps) pinned to eu-west with strict residency enabled.
2) Wait for a control-plane pin-refresh window (the customer noted ~every 15m refresh).
3) Observe elevated p95 and occasional 502s for ~10-30s during/after refresh.

Observed behavior:
- Latency spike at p95 from ~230ms to ~1.8s for a subset of requests.
- 502 responses correlate with TLS close alerts and short TCP resets seen in customer NAT logs.
- Traceroutes show an extra hop through a partner transit region (us-east) for affected requests.

Expected behavior:
- Pin refresh should be transparent to ongoing requests; no cross-region hairpin or TLS resets should occur.

Logs & metrics attached by customer (summarized):
- NAT logs: TCP RST events timestamped during refresh window.
- Support traces: examples of request IDs with 502s: req-55b3, req-55d1.
- Control-plane audit: pin-refresh events at 12:03:10Z, 12:18:10Z.

Investigation notes (initial):
- Hypothesis A: During control-plane pin refresh we briefly advertise a public egress that results in route asymmetry and forces traffic to traverse the customer's NAT -> partner transit -> back to eu-west instance (hairpin), adding latency and occasionally breaking TLS session reuse.
- Hypothesis B: Connection draining combined with NAT ephemeral ports exhaustion causes TLS session negotiation failures, surfacing as 502s.
- Observed flow logs from our edge show a subset of connections for the pinned tenant re-resolve the egress IP and select a different path while in-flight.

What we tried so far:
- SRE reproduced a pin-refresh in a staging private network with a simulated NAT and saw similar hairpin trace.
- Added extra logging in edge proxy for TLS handshake timing and session reuse; captured multiple full handshakes during refresh window.
- Coordinated with customer to temporarily disable NAT port reuse; RSTs reduced but latencies persisted for hairpinned flows.

Temporary workaround for customer:
- Schedule pin-refresh to off-peak windows (we can trigger manual pin refreshes on request).
- Optionally switch to Redwood-managed egress for the affected service to avoid asymmetric routing (not suitable for customer due to audit requirements).

Next steps / action items:
- [SRE] (Liam) Capture full packet capture during next scheduled refresh window (ETA 2026-03-13 09:00Z).
- [Networking] (Maya) Validate BGP advertisement ordering and egress prioritization in control-plane to prevent transient multi-region advertisement.
- [Product] (Priya) Discuss longer-term option: pin-refresh that preserves existing advertised egress until flows drain (graceful advertisement swap).
- [Customer] (BrightCart) Provide NAT gateway capacity and ephemeral port utilization metrics for 12:00-12:30Z on 2026-03-12.

Acceptance criteria for resolution:
- No TLS session resets tied to pin refresh windows and p95 falls back to baseline within 10s.
- Customer confirms reduced error rate to <0.1% during refresh windows for two consecutive refresh cycles.

Resolution notes (partial):
- Identified that our control-plane temporarily reweight advertisements during pin refresh which allowed a partner transit to be preferred; working on a control-plane fix to maintain egress affinity until existing sessions complete.
